decisions.decision: The rollback design keeps deadlines as optional fields in the version 1 data file and accepts that a save by 1.4.0 can strip deadlines while retaining the tickets.
decisions.alternative: They may have expected operators to be able to run 1.4.0 normally during a rollback and later upgrade again with the original deadlines intact, including for tickets whose priorities changed.

decisions.decision: The response targets count elapsed hours around the clock, including nights, weekends, and holidays.
decisions.alternative: They may have meant hours when the help desk is open, so tickets created outside staffed hours would get later deadlines.

decisions.decision: Backfill assigns each existing ticket a deadline based on its original creation time and the priority stored on the ticket when backfill runs.
decisions.alternative: They may have meant to use the ticket's priority at creation, recovered from its history when it has since changed.

decisions.decision: The new release assigns and stores deadlines when tickets are created even while DUE_TIMES is off, so tickets created during staging lock in the settings in effect at creation.
decisions.alternative: They may have wanted staging to defer assignment so tickets created while the feature is off receive deadlines under the settings chosen for production activation.

decisions.decision: Operators must stop the service that owns the file and run a separate, single-writer backfill command before starting the service with deadlines enabled.
decisions.alternative: They may have expected the new service to migrate the file automatically during startup before opening its listener, avoiding a separate operator command.

decisions.decision: If DUE_TIMES is enabled and any saved ticket lacks a deadline, the service refuses to listen.
decisions.alternative: They may have wanted the service to stay available with legacy responses and log that deadline activation is pending until the file has been backfilled.

decisions.decision: The work is delivered locally with a local rehearsal and production instructions, and the service operators own the production rollout.
decisions.alternative: They may have expected delivery to include carrying out and verifying the production backfill and activation with the appropriate access.

decisions.decision: The help desk changes response hours through optional, validated environment overrides, following the service's startup configuration model.
decisions.alternative: They may have wanted an administrative setting the help desk could change while the service is running, with the new targets taking effect for subsequent tickets without a restart.

decisions.decision: Backfill preserves ticket update timestamps and existing audit history and adds no audit entry for deadline assignment.
decisions.alternative: They may have wanted an appended audit entry recording when each ticket acquired its deadline and who ran the backfill.

decisions.decision: The overdue filter narrows the live legacy match set, so a request with both status and priority can return an active overdue ticket that matches either of those two filters.
decisions.alternative: They may have expected an overdue listing to require every supplied filter to match, following the documented combination rule.

decisions.decision: With deadlines enabled, the API includes due on every response that returns a ticket, including create, edit, and transition responses.
decisions.alternative: They may have meant to expose due on ticket reads while retaining the existing response shapes for write operations.

decisions.decision: With deadlines enabled, the human-readable CLI list and detail views show the due time.
decisions.alternative: They may have intended the new field for HTTP clients only, leaving the operator CLI display as it is.

decisions.decision: The existing raw CLI output keeps its four columns and the weekly report keeps its current output.
decisions.alternative: They may have wanted a fifth raw column for due, keeping the first four positions stable so scripts can start consuming deadlines.

decisions.decision: The API represents due as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC, following the convention for existing ticket timestamps.
decisions.alternative: They may have wanted the API to include the help desk's local UTC offset so clients can display the promised wall-clock time directly.

decisions.decision: The overdue check runs before cursor pagination, so page size and the next cursor are determined from matching overdue tickets.
decisions.alternative: They may have wanted overdue to hide rows within the existing ticket pages while retaining those pages' cursor boundaries.

decisions.decision: Each overdue page is evaluated against the clock for that request, so a later page can include tickets that became overdue during the traversal.
decisions.alternative: They may have wanted a single cutoff fixed on the first page so a multi-page scan uses the same definition of overdue throughout.

decisions.decision: A ticket becomes overdue strictly after its due timestamp passes.
decisions.alternative: They may have wanted the ticket to count as overdue at the exact instant it is due.
